Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT or THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OF THE SQETARY OPINION NO, 13 S. 2005 February 11, 2005 VICE MAYOR LUIS C. FAVORITO Taysan, Batangas Dear Vice Mayor Favorito: This pertains to your letter seeking our legal opinion anent the letter of Mayor Anacorita P. Portugal to all the members of the Sangguniang Bayan of that municipality denouncing the private employment with Fortune Cement Corporation of SB Member Edilberto Abaday. In reply thereto, please be informed that Section 90 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) provides that "Sanggunian members may practice their professions, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools except during session hours, xxx" From the fdregoing, it is clear that sangguniang bayan members are allowed to engage in any occupation, provided it is done during hours when no session is being conducted. In addition, although they are allowed to do so under Section 90 (b) of the Local Government Code, Section 7 of RA 6713 otherwise known as the Code of Ethical Standards for Government Officials and Employees, must still be considered. It provides that: "SECTION 7 - PROHIBITED ACTS AND TRANSACTIONS (b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto- Public officials and employees during their incumbency shall not: I) own, control, manage, or accept employfrlent as officer, employee, consultant, counsel, broker, agent, trustee, or nominee in any private enterprise regulated, supervised or licensed by their office unless expressly allowed by law; 2) engage in the practice of their profession unless authorized by the constitution or law, provided that such practice will not conflict or tend to conflict with their official functions; or 3) recommend any person to any position in a private enterprise which has a regular or pending official transaction with their office.

-2- The prohibitions shall continue to apply for a period of one year after resignation, retirement, or separation from public office, except in the case of subparagraph (b) (2) above, but the professional concerned cannot practice his profession in connection with any matter before the office he used to be with, in which case the one year prohibition shall likewise apply". Accordingly, elective local officials are allowed to engage in private undertakings provided that they will comply With the requirements under Section 90 of the Code and that such engagement will not constitute a violation of Section 7 of RA 6713. May it be noted further that while it is true that public official can be allowed to engage in private employment, they are not however allowed to engage in public employment in view of the express prohibition under Section 94 of RA 7160, which states that: "Section 94 (a) — No elective or appointive local officials shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no elective or appointive local official shall hotd any other office or employment in the government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporation or their subsidiaries. In this regard, w? are of the view that there is no legal impediment for Sangguniang Bayan Member Abaday's employment at Fortune Cement Corporation as long as it does not affect his attendance during session days or violate the conflict-of-interest rule as said employment is a private one. What is prohibited under Section 94 (a) is the employment of either an elective or appointive official in a public office, including GOCCs and its subsidiaries. Hope we have enlightened you on the matter. r. Leoni Io LG Region B. Lariosa IV-A Very truly yours, ANGEL T. REYES Secretary OF MERJOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT 'N Pts CITE; S!LG05-004223
